newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Foreign sales boost Audi first half.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Foreign sales boost Audi first half.

text.p: German luxury carmaker Audi AG said on Friday that group pre-tax profit climbed 20.9 percent in the first half of this year to 489 million marks ($262.2 million), driven by strong foreign demand.

Audi, the luxury car arm Volkswagen AG, said group sales increased 13.7 percent during the first half of the year to 10.6 billion marks -- an increase that analysts said came largely on the back of its mainstay A4 saloon.
Chairman Franz-Josef Paefgen said in a statement that the company was looking "with cautious optimism" to the future, but that weak economic growth, especially at home, was dampening sales.
The increase, however, marked continued solid sales growth at Audi which had reported a 47 percent increase in pre-tax profit in 1996 to 862 million marks.

Audi group deliveries during the fist half climbed 12.6 percent to 276,052, on pace for a company target this year of at least 500,000 deliveries. German deliveries climbed 10.5 percent to 121,835 units.
Audi also is doing well in the United States, the world's largest car market and an area of difficulty for the company until the last year or two.
Audi had previously reported it sold 17,019 new vehicles in the U.S., an increase of 34 percent and its best performance there in 10 years.
Demand also increased in western Europe excluding Germany. Deliveries climbed 14 percent to 111,045 units.
The carmaker did especially well in its home market, boosting its share of the market here to 6.8 percent from 5.8 percent at the same time in 1996.
Late last month, Audi arch-rival BMW AG said it too had increased its share of the German market to 6.5 percent from 6.1 percent.
Audi also continued to maintain its brisk investment pace, increasing investment 53.4 percent to 741 million marks.
The carmaker has said in the past it plans investments of six billion marks up to the year 2000, financed entirely without interest-bearing loans.
Audi's success comes as good news for parent Volkswagen which has seen its sales slump as the company prepares to introduce a new Golf model later this year.
